strengths: Clear and well-motivated core insight about disentangling static domain information from time-varying properties through lagged context prediction
Elegant and intuitive solution design with solid information-theoretic justification and illustrative toy case
Comprehensive experimental validation with multiple environments, morphological variations, detailed ablations (Table 2 and 4), and effective visualization of representation quality improvements
Strong reproducibility: detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, pseudocode, and promise to release code/datasets
Honest discussion of limitations, particularly the restriction to stationary environments
Demonstrates that representation quality improvements translate to practical policy performance gains through the mastery metric and online adaptation visualizations
weaknesses: Inconsistent empirical results across tasks: HalfCheetah OOD shows regression (3001 vs Meta-DT 3174), and improvements are task-dependent without clear analysis of when/why method succeeds or fails
Theoretical gaps: the claim that ∆t→∞ forces learning only static information lacks formal proof; bounded mutual information does not guarantee the encoder discards time-varying information
Limited technical novelty: Lagged Context is intuitive but straightforward; mixed Gaussian prior is adapted from existing Mixed DDIM; main contribution (Eq. 13) is incremental reformulation
Lack of principled guidance for selecting ∆t in practice; using ∆t→∞ requires sampling from other episodes, which is context-dependent and dataset-specific
Modest improvements in many cases (Ant and HalfCheetah nearly tied with baselines), suggesting limited robustness and unclear scope of applicability

Missing analysis of why Supervised baseline achieves comparable performance despite ground-truth labels (Table 4), raising questions about representation quality translation and potential representation ceiling issues
Significant practical limitation: restriction to stationary dynamics; many real environments have non-stationary properties (wear, temperature effects) that could be important

Baseline adaptation concerns: Prompt-DT modified to use online history instead of expert prompts may disadvantage baseline; no direct comparison with MetaDiffuser despite claiming it has entangled representations

strengths: Clear motivation for the problem: temporal proximity in context causes representation entanglement between static domain factors and time-varying properties is well-illustrated (especially in Appendix A toy example)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple environments (4 locomotion + 2 manipulation), both IID and OOD settings, detailed ablations, good visualizations of learned representations
Strong representation quality improvements demonstrated in Table 2: both linear probe accuracy and reconstruction loss consistently improve with larger Δt, approaching supervised performance
Excellent reproducibility support: extensive implementation details, complete hyperparameters (Table 6), detailed data generation procedures, promised code release
Honest discussion of limitations: authors acknowledge focus on stationary dynamics and articulate clear future directions
weaknesses: Statistical significance concerns: only 5 random seeds used; many reported improvements fall within error margins (e.g., HalfCheetah OOD: DADP 3001±225 vs Meta-DT 3174±501 are overlapping). No significance tests provided. OOD results—most critical for domain adaptation—show inconsistent or marginal improvements

Weak theoretical justification: (1) Information-theoretic argument asserting I(ωt; z_t-Δt | s_t, a_t, ξ) ≤ I(ωt; τ_t-Δt | s_t, a_t, ξ) lacks rigorous derivation; (2) Claim that averaged time-varying components (ω̄) produce 'static' representations is conceptually problematic; (3) Equation (6)'s 'natural global minimum' claim lacks formal justification

Unclear source of performance gains: Table 3 shows Meta-DT + larger Δt yields modest improvements, suggesting lagged context contributes incrementally. Table 4 reveals End-to-End Diffusion achieves comparable performance (3722/2852 on Walker2d) without explicit domain representation, contradicting claims about representation importance. Ablations don't isolate component contributions

Internal contradictions about representation properties: Appendix C.2 shows different context sources (Cold Start, Persistent, Warm Start) yield similar performance (~0.85 normalized return), undermining the claim that learned representations are specifically 'static domain information'

Insufficient out-of-distribution validation: improvements in OOD settings (most relevant for domain adaptation) are often small or absent; no analysis of actual out-of-distribution distance or failure modes

Ad-hoc diffusion formulation: reformulation from Eq. (12) to Eq. (13) bundling noise and representation shift lacks clear justification for why networks should predict this specific composite term. Claim of 'extra supervision' appears to be mathematical reformulation rather than functional difference

Modest and inconsistent empirical gains: Walker2d OOD shows DADP 2834±285, Hopper and Adroit show minimal differences, and some results have overlapping confidence intervals with baselines. Limited novelty—combines existing ideas (lagged contexts, diffusion priors from MetaDiffuser) without substantial conceptual innovation

Incomplete experimental analysis: (1) No guidance on selecting Δt in practice (critical hyperparameter?); (2) No computational cost comparison; (3) Baseline modifications (Prompt-DT adapted to zero-shot) may not reflect original method design; (4) Supervised baseline achieves only 99.3-99.9% rather than 100%, suggesting representation space limitations

Presentation issues: overstated claims ('superior performance' when results overlap error bars), inconsistent notation (z_t vs z_t-Δt vs z_-∞), unmotivated 'mastery' metric (why 60% threshold?), difficult-to-read t-SNE visualizations, scattered experimental details across appendices

strengths: Clear problem motivation with intuitive solution: the lagged context mechanism elegantly removes time-varying information by breaking temporal correlation between context and prediction target
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 environments with both IID and OOD settings, showing consistent improvements and better stability than baselines
Thorough ablation studies examining the effect of Δt on representation quality (Table 2), different utilization strategies (Table 4), and practical flexibility (context source variants)
Strong representation quality analysis with clear progressive improvement in linear probe accuracy and domain clustering as Δt increases
Practical contributions including detailed hyperparameters, pseudocode, and promise of open-source release for reproducibility
Effective presentation with illustrative visualizations, particularly Figure 2 showing the denoising process and toy example in Appendix A
weaknesses: Weak theoretical justification for core mechanism: the information-theoretic argument for why lagged contexts remove time-varying information is intuitive but not rigorously proven; claims about 'static' representations are overstated given that averaged varying properties still vary across domains

Mixed experimental results undermine claims of consistent superiority: notable underperformance on some tasks (e.g., HalfCheetah OOD: 3001 vs Meta-DT 3174; Door IID: 1428 vs Prompt-DT 2116); no statistical significance testing despite large standard deviations
Limited novelty in diffusion component: mixed Gaussian priors are not new (builds on Jia et al., 2024), and the joint prediction objective is an incremental modification of existing techniques

Overstated claims about disentanglement: the paper does not rigorously prove separation of static and dynamic information; gaps to supervised learning (Table 2: 99.3% vs 99.8%) and inconsistency with Table 4 results undermine claims of 'comparable' performance
Significant limitation to stationary dynamics restricts real-world applicability; many practical scenarios involve non-stationary environments with evolving dynamics

Missing critical analyses: no computational cost comparison, no sensitivity to history length H, no evaluation with fewer training domains, no quantified failure case analysis, and no statistical significance testing for reported improvements

strengths: Clear and well-motivated core insight: Lagged Context Dynamical Prediction effectively disentangles static domain information from transient properties, with strong empirical validation showing monotonic improvements (Table 2) approaching supervised performance

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 environments (4 MuJoCo + 2 Adroit) with three evaluation settings (Seen/Unseen/OOD), multiple metrics, and consistent improvements with tight error bars across 5 seeds
Novel and transferable representation learning approach: Δt → ∞ strategy is simple yet effective, with demonstrated transferability to other policy architectures (Meta-DT ablation in Table 6)

Practical enhancements with real-world applicability: Robustness to non-stationary dynamics (C.5), strong one-step DDIM performance (C.6), and thorough ablation studies isolating each component's contribution

Reproducibility support: Comprehensive implementation details (Table 5), pseudocode (Algorithm 1), promised code/dataset release, and direct evidence of disentanglement via within-domain std analysis (Table 12)
weaknesses: Insufficient theoretical justification: The information-theoretic argument in Section 4.1 lacks formal proof. The claim that I(ωt; z_{t-Δt} | st, at, ξ) ≤ I(ωt; τ_{t-Δt} | st, at, ξ) is stated without derivation; the definition of 'averaged varying properties' ω̄ when Δt → ∞ is vague

Ambiguous test-time implementation: The critical detail that contexts are sampled 'from another episode in the same domain' is not clearly specified—whether this requires a domain-specific replay buffer, how it's accessed at test time, and whether this constitutes a form of access to target domain data needs clarification in main text (buried in C.3)

Ad-hoc diffusion formulation: The reformulation in Eq. (13) combining representation and noise (ϵ̂_θ = √(1-ᾱk)·z + √(1-ᾱk)·ϵ) lacks rigorous justification for why this specific form is optimal or how it differs from simpler alternatives

Problematic experimental comparisons: (1) Supervised baseline comparison is unfair—it uses access to ground-truth environment parameters/domain indices; (2) MetaDiffuser, the most relevant baseline, compared only indirectly via ablations due to unavailable code; (3) Benchmark construction (introduction of morphological variations) may favor DADP's approach

Limited novelty and modest improvements on benchmarks: Diffusion injection is relatively straightforward (substituting representations into equations); improvements on some environments (Hopper Seen: 44% vs baseline, but only ~47% vs expert) suggest limited gains; Adroit evaluation is minimal (3 domains total, 2 train/1 test)

strengths: Clear motivation for the problem: the paper identifies that dynamical prediction entangles static domain information with time-varying properties, illustrated well with the projectile motion toy case
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple environments (4 MuJoCo + Adroit), evaluation settings (Seen/Unseen/OOD), and careful ablations with proper error bars and random seeds
Strong empirical results especially on out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, showing consistent advantages over baselines including SOTA Meta-DT

Thorough ablation studies examining effect of Δt on representation quality, different utilization strategies, generality to other architectures (Meta-DT), and practical considerations (non-stationary dynamics, one-step inference)
Good reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, pseudocode, and commitment to release code and datasets
Introduces interpretable metrics for representation quality (linear probe accuracy, reconstruction loss, within-domain std) that directly measure disentanglement
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual components: lagged context is straightforward (sampling from different episodes), and diffusion injection builds directly on Mixed DDIM (Jia et al. 2024); the combination is new but feels incremental

Weak theoretical justification for Δt → ∞: the key claim that I(ωt; zt−Δt | st, at, ξ) ≤ I(ωt; τt−Δt | st, at, ξ) is asserted without proof, and there is no formal analysis of when disentanglement succeeds or fails

Critical missing comparison: MetaDiffuser (most relevant baseline that also injects representations into diffusion) cannot be compared directly because it is not open-sourced; indirect comparison via ablations is insufficient for a venue like ICML

Hopper results reveal significant method limitations: linear probe accuracy is only 26.4% at Δt → ∞ versus 99% for other environments, contradicting claims of parameter-free universal performance; explanation (no morphological variations) is unsatisfying

End-to-End Diffusion baseline performs surprisingly well (Table 3), sometimes within 5-8% of DADP on Seen tasks, raising questions about whether the added complexity is necessary and what portion of gains comes from representations versus diffusion injection

Overstated claims: The method is described as parameter-free and universal, but requires environment-specific guidance scale tuning (Table 7: 0.05 for Ant, 0.1 for others) and shows highly variable performance across environments

Restrictive problem formulation: explicitly limited to stationary dynamics with parameter-only variation (same task type, different dynamics); real-world domain shift often involves changes to rewards, observation distributions, or action spaces

Incomplete representation utility analysis: while linear probe accuracy is reported, the causal connection between better clustering and downstream policy performance is assumed rather than validated; Figure 4 visualization is not a rigorous justification
Adroit evaluation underdeveloped: only 2-3 training domains (vs. 25 for MuJoCo), no ablations, and limited analysis of whether findings transfer to manipulation tasks

Missing key details for reproducibility: unclear exactly how context is sampled during evaluation when Δt → ∞; no analysis of sensitivity to context length (H=16), prediction horizon (4), and other hyperparameter choices

strengths: Clear problem identification: Paper articulates a genuine limitation where standard dynamical prediction entangles static domain factors with time-varying properties, confusing policies during adaptation
Well-motivated and elegant solution: LCDP is intuitive with good toy-case intuition in Appendix A; insight that sampling from different episodes achieves ∆t→∞ is practical
Technically sound: Reformulation of diffusion with mixture-of-Gaussians prior (Eqs. 9-14) is mathematically rigorous; joint prediction objective cleverly combines supervision
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple environments (4 MuJoCo + 2 Adroit), three difficulty settings (Seen/Unseen/OOD), strong baselines, thorough ablations validating both components

Consistent and strong empirical results: Particularly impressive on OOD tasks; smaller variance across seeds indicates stability; handles non-stationary dynamics and achieves competitive one-step generation
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Informative visualizations, detailed hyperparameters and pseudocode, honest limitation discussion, promised open-source release
Demonstrated generality: LCDP benefits transfer to Meta-DT (Table 6), showing the representation learning technique is not specific to diffusion policies
weaknesses: Incomplete theoretical justification: Information-theoretic argument I(ωt; zt−∆t | st, at, ξ) ≤ I(ωt; τt−∆t | st, at, ξ) stated without proof; connection between ∆t→∞ and cross-episode sampling needs formal establishment; 'averaged varying properties ω̄' explanation is hand-wavy

Insufficient comparison with closest work: MetaDiffuser (Ni et al., 2023) not directly compared due to lack of open source; indirect comparison via ablations (∆t=1 vs ∆t=∞) is insufficient for establishing relative merit

Limited failure mode analysis: Hopper achieves only 26.4% probe accuracy at ∆t→∞ (vs 99.3% Walker2d) raising questions about when LCDP degrades; insufficient discussion of dataset/domain properties LCDP depends on
Scope confined to offline meta-RL: No evaluation on online adaptation or continual learning; unclear how method generalizes beyond this setting
Unjustified design choices: Representation dimension set to dim(s)+dim(a) without ablation; Transformer encoder architecture not justified; mastery metric (60% threshold) appears post-hoc
Statistical rigor concerns: No statistical significance tests despite overlapping error bars in some cases (e.g., HalfCheetah Seen); modest improvements relative to variance on some tasks
Missing computational analysis: Context encoder training costs and total training time overhead versus baselines not reported; scalability with number of domains not discussed
Limited reward variation experiments: Main results focus exclusively on dynamics variation; Appendix C.1 shows mixed results for reward changes, limiting generality claims
